To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adipokines adiponectin, leptin and resistin are altered in patients with type 2 diabetic nephropathy and that these changes are related to the degree of kidney function impairment.
the adipokine leptin is a key player in the pathogenesis of DN.
adipokines are dysregulated in diabetes and are involved in the pathogenesis of DN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach in the treatment of diabetic nephropathy by the administration of the adipokines adiponectin and resistin, or leptin, in combination with a dietary intervention.
the effect of a low-carbohydrate, high-fat diet on renal function in diabetic patients, and whether it can be considered an alternative to a low-fat diet in the treatment of diabetic nephropathy.
the role of adipokines (leptin, adiponectin, and resistin) in the pathogenesis of diabetes mellitus (DM) and its complications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evidence is not sufficient to support the use of any of the dietary supplements reviewed in this article as an effective treatment of diabetic nephropathy, but that the evidence is insufficient to exclude their use as well.
the evidence is inadequate to determine if the use of a low-fat diet is effective in reducing blood glucose and A1C in people with type 2 diabetes.
there is no evidence to support or refute the use of vitamin E supplementation in the treatment of patients with diabetes mellitus and diabetic neuropathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of our research indicate that adiponectin, leptin and resistin are involved in the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy, and their serum concentrations are altered in response to the treatment of diabetes and/or hypertension.
the results of our research indicate that the expression of leptin and resistin in diabetic nephropathies is significantly upregulated.
the results of the present study indicate that a low-carbohydrate diet is an effective treatment for type 2 diabetes and is well tolerated in the short term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adiponectin and leptin are associated with the development of DN.
we have shown that the adipokines leptin, resistin, and adiponectin have different responses to dietary intervention in the diabetic nephropathy (DN) rat model.
adiponectin and resistin are both involved in the regulation of renal function in diabetic nephropathic rats.
